articles.title: Iran says that diplomatic efforts have been "active" in recent days, received proposals from several mediators
articles.description: The good news at least is that there is some form of exchange in order to try and de-escalate, with Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson Baghaei insisting that a "binary choice of negotiations or war is not useful". He maintains that "diplomacy does not negate defense" and that "defense is not incompatible with diplomacy". Adding that Iran has received several proposals from mediators for the resumption of negotiations. As much as the headlines might point to some return to optimism, it is still too early to prejudge anything. As mentioned before, nuclear/uranium negotiations are not going to amount to anything as there are still key red lines that are holding for both sides. And in the bigger picture, this is exactly what Iran wants. That is to keep playing for time and to drag all of this out over and over and for as long as they can. From before: Iran's strategy in leveraging on control over the Strait of Hormuz looks to be working Baghaei goes on to say that US talks might be possible if and only if though they are pursued on the basis of national interests. As much as both sides can talk the talk, I can foresee negotiations breaking down again the minute missile strikes are exchanged once more. And with Iran not going to relent on giving up control over the Strait of Hormuz, I don't see how things will be any much different from what they were in the past few weeks. If anything, it could just be a case of Groundhog Day for markets as we continue to repeatedly take one step back and then one foot forward again. This article was written by Justin Low at investinglive.com.

articles.title: 'So psycho': Outrage as Trump belts out another 'dumb and horrible' war claim
articles.description: President Donald Trump let fly another claim about the war against Iran that outraged observers on Sunday. Trump was greeted by reporters at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland after he returned home from attending the World Cup Final in New York earlier in the day. During a quick press conference, the president was asked about the progress of the war. His answers seemed to upset several people who watched the event. "Mr. President, you said at the start of the war that it would be four or five weeks ..." the reporter began, shouting over the humming engines of the presidential helicopter, Marine One. "Well, this is a far bigger job that we're doing," Trump interjected. "We were doing a little job, stopping them from having a certain capability. Now, we're just ending it. So, it's really not the same thing." Trump's comments horrified political analysts and observers, who shared their reactions on social media. "Pete Hegseth has convinced this demented moron that he can “win” if he just sends ground troops and uses the rest of our munitions. This is so psycho," Jim Stewartson, a political commentator and writer, posted to his more than 151,000 followers on X. "He also said 53 times that the Ukraine war would end 24 hours into taking office," Dan Koh, a former Biden administration staffer who is running for Congress in Massachusetts, told his more than 25,000 followers on X. "What a dumb and horrible human being. Not a political message by me. Just an objective fact," Ben Meiselas, founder of MeidasTouch, posted to his 285,000 followers on X. "The 'far bigger job' is un-f------ the Strait he messed up for no reason," the liberal outlet The Tennessee Holler posted to its 302,000 followers on X.
